html:
The Abd al-Wadids, also called the Zayyanids, were a Zenata Berber dynasty that ruled the Kingdom of Tlemcen in western Algeria. They are shown here in 1279, early in their history; the map places them a little to the west. Their later years are on the page Zayyanid Kingdom of Tlemcen.

Their founder, Yaghmurasen ibn Zayyan, had governed Tlemcen for the Almohads and made himself independent in 1235. Tlemcen sat where caravan routes from the Sahara met the road to the coast, and it grew rich on the trans-Saharan trade in gold.

Squeezed between the Marinids of Morocco and the Hafsids of Tunis, the kingdom was often attacked. The Marinids besieged Tlemcen for about eight years, from 1299, and occupied it twice in the 14th century. Each time the Zayyanids came back.
